notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Single yellow edge lines with white centre lines on most roads; neighbouring southern African countries do this too.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Rare triple centre lines: two solid white outside a dashed white, or two white with one yellow in the middle. Only the neighbours share these.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 2 is common here: big round car blur and halo colour distortion in the sky. It is the only Generation 2 in Africa.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: All Generation 4 coverage uses a blue car with a short antenna, sometimes hidden by the blur, plus some low-mounted smallcam coverage.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Eleven official languages; the lingua franca dominates signs, and a Dutch-related language shows up in place names ending -fontein, -kraal, -kop, -dorp, -nek and -berg.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: The most common pole has 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that look like rows of birds.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green direction signs with yellow road numbers; N and R roads exist only here.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Triangular warning signs with a red border and white background, shared with the neighbours.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: White-and-red chevrons, plus small thin one-arrow chevrons next to roads.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Suburban houses in big cities are surrounded by high walls, fences and gates.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Each province has its own plate design; Free State plates look slightly green and KwaZulu-Natal ones slightly blue.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Phone numbers are 10 digits, and the 2nd and 3rd digits of the landline code give the area; mobile numbers start 06 to 08.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with three bars forming an A, the lower insulators on a horizontal bar, are almost only in the Western Cape.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A wider A-shaped top with insulators attached directly to the A marks the Eastern Cape.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with three alternating side insulators are mostly in Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with one or two metal arms holding insulators are most common in Mpumalanga.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Square red stickers on the back of ordinary signs are common in the Eastern Cape and nearby parts of the Northern Cape and Free State.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Grainy, Texas-like pavement with a pink hint is found in Limpopo.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Big bird nests on poles are common in the north of the Northern Cape.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The northeast can look dry and barren with orange or red soil and shrub-covered hills, but very green in wet season.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rocky, treeless mountains with tall steep sides and sharp peaks are in the Western Cape; vineyards are mostly here too.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dry landscape with red soil is typical of the Northern Cape; vineyards also grow near Upington.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Sugarcane is common in KwaZulu-Natal, mainly along the coast, and in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Very tall Cook pines grow mostly along the southeast coast between East London and Durban.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Pine plantations are common west of Eswatini and in the south of KwaZulu-Natal.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: A flat savannah with dry grass, small trees, no farms and red soil under the grass surrounds the big wildlife park; a camouflage car appears there.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Traffic lights and crossing poles in the biggest city are wrapped in three strips of reflective tape.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Dodgy adverts for medical services and pills are plastered on poles in and around Gauteng.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A prominent flat plateau about 3 km long, flanked by a pyramid-shaped peak, rises by the Western Cape coast.
